name: lamination-fold-shear
title: Lamination Fold Shear
description: A multi-stage pipeline/onboarding stepper rendered as a croissant-dough cross-section: a butter block enclosed in dough passes through three letter-folds, each fold tripling the visible layer count (1 -> 3 -> 9 -> 27) as every existing butter hairline splits into three during a whole-stack shear pass, then a geometric wipe merges the stack back to one layer and the cycle folds again.
useWhen: a multi-stage stepper or pipeline-progress indicator (deploy stages, onboarding steps, build steps) where the number of visible sub-steps genuinely multiplies at each stage rather than just advancing a pointer along a fixed row of dots — the mechanic is literal band-count tripling at a fold instant (1/3/9/27), never a falloff curve or a continuous draw. Reach for carbon-ply-fade instead when the surface is a static row of N fixed slots whose registered density decays by a fixed ratio down the stack on every new event — no row ever splits into more rows. Reach for float-ribbon-draw instead when the process is a single continuous, non-restructuring draw (one fixed thermal gradient scrolling at a constant rate) rather than a discrete multiply-then-reset cycle. Reach for stepper-needle or stepper-ratchet instead for a bounded numeric input control, not a status/pipeline display.
instruction: Build <LaminationFoldShear steps? activeStep? label? className?> as a self-contained 2D canvas widget inside a bordered card (rounded-md border border-border bg-surface, 16:10 canvas aspect-ratio, geometry derived from the container's smaller dimension: bandUnit = minDim / 64, and the laminate stack's height = clamp(32 * bandUnit, 81px floor, 80% of card height) so the pitch between hairlines never falls below ~3 CSS px even at 27 layers — the number that must stay legible is pitch, not band-fill height). The stack is drawn side-view: a dough FILL (lerp of --background toward --ns-muted at t=0.12, near-background luminance) with N butter hairlines drawn as STROKES (never fills) at evenly spaced y-fractions, stroke width = max(0.6px floor, 4px / N) so widths run 4 -> 1.33 -> 0.44 -> floored-to-0.6 across the three folds. CYCLE (unbounded, 9200ms, performance.now()-based modulo): fold 1 [0,2300) = a 1400ms shear pass splitting N=1 into N=3 followed by a 900ms rest; fold 2 [2300,4600) splits 3 into 9; fold 3 [4600,6900) splits 9 into 27; a 1500ms hold at 27 layers [6900,8400); an 800ms geometric wipe [8400,9200) that merges 27 back to 1 via a vertical sweep line — canvas regions left of the sweep are clipped and re-rendered at N=1, regions right of it still render at N=27, a real spatial merge rather than an opacity cascade (opacity cascades read as carbon-ply-fade's propagating strike, which this must not resemble). FOLD SPLIT ANIMATION: each of the prevN hairlines occupies a 1/prevN-tall cell; during the 1400ms shear (eased with an easeInOutCubic on progress p), that one line becomes three — the centre child stays at the parent's exact y-position while its stroke width interpolates from the prior fold's width to the next fold's width, and the two outer children grow outward from that same starting position to their final resting points at the cell's 1/6 and 5/6 fractions, fading in via alpha = p as they travel, so the transition shows departure and arrival rather than a blink between two static line counts. Simultaneously, the WHOLE STACK undergoes a shear transform for the same 1400ms: skewX and a slight vertical-compress/horizontal-widen bump (both driven by sin(p * PI), so they peak mid-pass and relax back to identity exactly as the pass ends), applied via ctx.transform pivoted on the stack's own centre — this is decorative shear-pass flavour layered on top of, not instead of, the literal count-tripling animation. SEPARATORS: exactly two --border hairlines mark the fold-1 thirds (drawn always, at 1/3 and 2/3 of the stack height, plus a --border outer frame rect) — a fixed count regardless of layer depth, so structure reads at 3 and at 27 without ever multiplying into per-band barcode noise (kill criterion: never render finer than 27 layers, hard cap). REDUCED MOTION freezes at cycle t=6400ms (fold 3's rest phase: 27 layers fully settled, not mid-shear) by calling the same pure cycleState(t) function once at mount and painting it with no rAF loop ever started; the ResizeObserver and MutationObserver-driven token re-reads both repaint that same frozen state rather than silently going blank. TOKENS: --background, --ns-muted, --foreground, --border are each resolved once via getComputedStyle(document.documentElement) using the house parseColor/lerpColor/rgbStr idiom (hex or rgb() strings, no literal fallback colour), re-read on every documentElement class-attribute mutation via a MutationObserver, with no paint before the first successful read (the mount routine retries on the next rAF until tokens resolve) and a ResizeObserver keeping canvas pixel size/DPR in sync; an IntersectionObserver pauses the rAF loop off-screen and re-arms it (re-checking tokens for a theme flip that happened while hidden) on re-entry. INTERACTION (optional, off by default): an optional `steps` prop (up to 3 labels) renders a row of bordered button chips below the canvas, mirroring a real stepper's own focus chrome (border, focus-visible:outline-ns-accent) — accent is used only for that chip's own focus ring, never mixed into the lamination bands. Hovering or focusing a chip highlights that fold-1 third's hairlines by lifting them 45% toward --foreground in luminance only (never accent); an externally controlled `activeStep` prop does the same for a caller wiring this into a real deploy/onboarding pipeline. When `steps` is omitted the card is purely ambient with no interactive affordance. Cleanup on unmount cancels every pending rAF and disconnects all three observers.
